title: Northbridge FinServ POC - Benchmark Decomposition and Recommendations
content:
Executive summary:

This doc summarizes the benchmarking experiments we ran for the Northbridge Financial Services POC (conversational agent + document retrieval) and provides a decomposition of latency, throughput, and estimated unit cost across candidate deployment options (Hosted API vs Dedicated pool vs Private VPC). The goal: give a clear recommendation for an initial production-shaped configuration and a low-risk rollout plan to meet SLAs (p50 latency < 120ms token, p95 < 350ms token for short-turn interactions) while bounding cost for the pilot.

Scope and success criteria:
- Workload: customer chatbot that handles short transactions and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) across 2–5 document snippets. Typical prompts are 60–180 tokens input, expected outputs 80–400 tokens.
- Traffic profile (POC): 150 concurrent users, average 1.6 requests/minute/user -> sustained 4 RPS, with 8x burst windows up to 32 RPS for flash support tests.
- Success criteria: p50 < 120ms (per-token), p95 < 350ms for single-request median path; throughput to support 32 RPS with graceful degradation; estimated hosted cost <= $0.35 per 1k tokens for pilot (target).

Test harness and methodology:
- Testbed: synthetic replay of customer traces (sanitized), warmed cache scenario (50% prefix cache hit), and cold start scenario.
- Hardware & deployment modes tested:
  - Hosted (Redwood managed): H100-80GB equivalent slots (shared noisy neighbors simulated)
  - Dedicated: 4x H100-80GB GPU pool (pinned to customer)
  - Private: single-node A100-40GB on customer-provided VPC (representative of small on-prem)
- Models evaluated: Mistral-Instruct-7B (float16 baseline), Redwood-7B-INT8 (quantized int8 variant), OpenLM-13B-llama2-compat (13B float16).
- Config knobs: streaming vs non-streaming, batch size (1, 4, 16), KV cache enabled/disabled, request chunking and max_tokens=512.
- Metrics captured: p50/p95 request latency (ms) measured as time-to-first-token (TTFT) and time-to-last-token (TTLT), tokens/sec throughput per GPU, end-to-end cost estimate (GPU runtime converted to $/1k tokens using current pricing model).

Key findings (high level):
1) For short interactive flows (avg 120 output tokens), quantized Redwood-7B-INT8 on Dedicated H100 pool provided the best p50 (approx 85ms TTFT) and p95 (210ms TTFT) while keeping cost per 1k tokens ~ $0.18 (pilot assumptions).
2) Mistral-Instruct-7B (float16) had similar perceived latency for single requests but consumed ~1.6x tokens/sec less throughput under batching, increasing cost to roughly $0.28/1k tokens when scaled to peak burst with the same hardware.
3) OpenLM-13B delivered higher answer quality on edge cases in our eval set but increased p95 latency by ~2.6x vs Redwood-7B-INT8 and raised estimated cost > $0.55/1k tokens. Not recommended for initial pilot where latency and cost are primary constraints.
4) Enabling prefix/KV caching produced the largest marginal wins for latency: p50 TTFT improvement of 35–45% on repeated flows and effective tokens/sec improvement of 1.8x in mixed traffic.
5) Batching benefits were very workload-dependent: for retrieval-heavy interactions (long context, >3 snippets) batching (4–16) increased throughput but caused p95 latency regressions for interactive requests. We recommend dynamic batching with strict latency SLOs (max batch wait 6ms).

Numeric summary (representative snapshots):
- Dedicated H100 + Redwood-7B-INT8 (warm cache, batch=1): p50 TTFT = 85ms, p95 TTFT = 210ms, throughput (tokens/sec/GPU) = 950, estimated cost = $0.18 / 1k tokens.
- Hosted (mixed tenants sim) + Redwood-7B-INT8 (warm, batch=1): p50 TTFT = 105ms, p95 TTFT = 320ms, throughput = 780 tps/GPU, cost = $0.23 / 1k tokens.
- Dedicated H100 + Mistral-7B (float16, batch=4): p50 TTFT = 110ms, p95 TTFT = 380ms, throughput = 520 tps/GPU, cost = $0.28 / 1k tokens.
- Private A100 + Redwood-7B-INT8 (cold cache, batch=1): p50 TTFT = 160ms, p95 TTFT = 440ms, throughput = 420 tps/GPU, cost = $0.35 / 1k tokens (includes additional infra latency).
- OpenLM-13B on Dedicated H100 (batch=1): p50 TTFT = 230ms, p95 TTFT = 560ms, throughput = 360 tps/GPU, cost = $0.57 / 1k tokens.

Latency decomposition and root causes:
- Token generation compute time: ~60% of p50 for quantized 7B models; for 13B models this becomes >80% of p50.
- KV cache and attention prep: for RAG flows, retrieving and serializing snippets adds 40–120ms depending on snippet count and I/O path; local caching reduces this to ~15–40ms.
- Scheduling and batching overhead: with strict latency SLOs and small batch windows, we observed a 6–12ms additional hop cost per request on the runtime; higher when queueing/batching is aggressive.
- Network and TLS: hosted vs private differences introduced a 12–35ms median delta when calling cross-region backplanes; colocated VPC reduces this but increases infra ops burden.

Quality vs latency tradeoffs:
- In automated evals on the Northbridge sample set (1.2k test prompts), OpenLM-13B scored ~3–5% better on domain-specific QA F1 and on hallucination detection. However, human review of typical short-form transactions showed marginal quality delta relative to Mistral-7B for the top 80% cases. Given the customer SLAs around response speed, we recommend prioritizing the 7B family for pilot and profiling any 13B use to specific high-value workflows.

Recommendations (POC -> Pilot):
1) Pilot baseline (recommended): Dedicated H100 pool, Redwood-7B-INT8, KV/prefix cache enabled, streaming with time-to-first-token streaming threshold set at 50ms, dynamic batching with max wait 6ms and max batch size 8. This balances p95/p50 with cost efficiency.
2) Fallback & tiering: Route low-latency transactions to 7B-INT8; route long-form or audit-required sessions to an isolated 13B model running on separate capacity (non-critical latency). Implement automatic fallback to smaller model when overall system load > 70% to maintain SLOs.
3) Observability: Add per-route token breakdowns (prompt tokens vs context tokens vs response tokens), cost at token-level, and drift detection tied to prompt set. Create dashboards for p50/p95 TTFT and TTLT per model variant.
4) Private deployment notes: If Northbridge requires private VPC, propose a dedicated two-node A100 cluster to start; expect ~1.8x higher cost per 1k tokens vs Redwood Dedicated but lower network egress risk. Plan for a hybrid approach (control plane hosted, runtime in VPC).

Risk and mitigations:
- Model regression during quantization: we observed a small drop in retrieval hallucination metrics for INT8 in adversarial prompts (~2–3%); mitigate by adding automated evals on production prompts and enabling automatic rollback to float16 if drift is detected.
- Sudden traffic spikes: set autoscaling thresholds and pre-warm capacity for close-of-business batch windows; implement rate-limited fallbacks and user-facing throttling to avoid latency cliffs.
- Data locality: if documents remain remote (customer DB calls), add local snippet caching layer to reduce fetch latency.

Next steps / action items (owners):
- Solutions eng (Samir): finalize pilot config and produce deployment runbook (NB-PILOT-DEPLOY) by 2026-03-18. Linked JIRA: JIRA-NB-87.
- Applied ML (Elena): run quantization safety sweep on 1k adversarial prompts and report regression risks by 2026-03-15.
- Eng infra (Marcus): size initial dedicated pool and provide cost estimate for a 3-month reserved window (due 2026-03-20).
- Customer success (Priya): coordinate pilot SLA sign-off and acceptance criteria with Northbridge legal/security (target meeting 2026-03-16).

Appendix A — Raw experiment notes and fringe observations:
- Cold start behavior: first request to an idle GPU often added 120–220ms; recommend warm pools or synthetic keep-alive during business hours.
- Streaming tradeoffs: for outputs >200 tokens, streaming reduced perceived latency significantly (TTFT) and improved user satisfaction in manual tests; however, it complicates streaming-bytes billing accounting—finance to confirm.
- Multi-model routing: simple policy using request metadata (priority tag + max_latency) allowed near-instant routing to dedicated low-latency pool for VIP users.

Appendix B — Representative commands & harness pointers:
- Perf runner used: https://github.com/redwood-inference/northbridge-poc (PR42)
- Confluence spec: CONFLUENCE-12345 (detailed test matrix and raw csv dumps)
- JIRA epic: JIRA-NB-87 (pilot orchestration)
